acquisition method: The 20 most intense signals above an intensity threshold of 104 and with charge states 2–5 were subjected to collision induced dissociation in the ion trap
alkylation reagent: free sulfhydryl groups were carbamidomethylated using 30 mM iodoacetamide for 30 min at room temperature in the dark
alkylation concentration: free sulfhydryl groups were carbamidomethylated using 30 mM iodoacetamide for 30 min at room temperature in the dark
cleavage agent: Trypsin (Promega, sequencing grade) was added at a ratio of 1:30 and incubated at 37 °C for 12 h
collision energy: normalized collision energy of 35%; normalized collision energy 30%
enrichment method: Separation of the three protein classes was achieved by either (i) carbonate treatment at pH 11.5 to separate integral membrane proteins (retained in the pellet, PELcarb) from peripheral membrane and soluble proteins (extracted into the supernatant, SNcarb) or (ii) sonication of the purified organelles to separate a complete membrane fraction (incl. integral and peripheral proteins; PELson) from the soluble proteins (SNson)
fractionation method: strong cation exchange chromatography (SCX); C18 column
fractionated using strong cation exchange chromatography (SCX); fractionated on a C18 column (Zorbax, I.D. 0.5 mm × 150 mm, Agilent) at pH 6.5
fragmentation method: collision induced dissociation; higher energy collisional dissociation
subjected to collision induced dissociation in the ion trap; fragmented by higher energy collisional dissociation
instrument: Nano-LC-MS/MS was performed on an LTQ-Orbitrap Elite mass spectrometer; Pooled samples were analyzed on a Q Exactive Plus as described above
labeling: We used stable isotope labeled yeast cultures (SILAC); compared their relative abundance within mitochondria and complete yeast cells, based on label free spectral counting
mass analyzer: subjected to collision induced dissociation in the ion trap
precursor tolerance: MS and MS/MS tolerances of 10 ppm and 0.5 Da, respectively
fragment tolerance: MS and MS/MS tolerances of 10 ppm and 0.5 Da, respectively
ptm: carbamidomethylation of cysteine (fixed); oxidation of methionine (variable); acetylation of protein N-termini (variable); 13C6 15N2 Lys (variable); 13C6 15N4 Arg (variable)
carbamidomethylation of cysteine as fixed and (iii) oxidation of methionine, acetylation of protein N-termini, 13C6 15N2 Lys and 13C6 15N4 Arg as variable modifications
reduction reagent: Cysteines were reduced with 10 mM DTT for 30 min at 56 °C
reduction concentration: Cysteines were reduced with 10 mM DTT for 30 min at 56 °C
